note: EVERY MODULE IS A ROW HERE, NOT A CONTROLLER. Adding a screen is an entry in this file; there is no PHP to write, which is the governing sentence of the rebuild made literal. A column named here that the table does not have is REFUSED at load, never skipped — a screen quietly missing a column is one nobody notices is broken.

fields_note: Add a `fields` object to any module to customise how it is edited. Every key is a column; every property is optional. label — what to call it in your words. type — text, number, date, datetime-local, time, email, tel, textarea, checkbox. options — turns it into a dropdown and REFUSES anything else. required — refused when empty, with the label in the message. readonly — shown, never written. hidden — kept off the form entirely. help — a line under the field. A key naming a column the table does not have is reported ON THE SCREEN, never silently dropped. lookup — {table, value, show[]} turns the field into a dropdown of rows from ANOTHER table, showing names instead of ids in BOTH the form and the list, and refusing an id that points at nothing. The list is read through the tenant-scoped store, because a dropdown is the easiest place to leak another customer's names. permissions — {view, edit} names the permission this module needs; 'can see the employee list' and 'can see everybody's salary' are not the same permission, and giving them one name is how the second gets granted by somebody who meant the first.
